messages:
Maria Chen: heads up — p99 latency for SplitStream (new model onboarding) jumped from ~420ms to ~1.8s for long inputs (>30k chars) after yesterday's tokenizer tweak. multiple customer reports. :frowning_face:
Kevin Patel: saw that in dashboards, correlates with spike in request backpressure and increased batching wait time. p95 also shifted a bit.
Ben Ortiz: any error logs or repro? can we repro locally with their payload?
Maria Chen: pasting a minimal repro we used against staging: 
```bash
curl -s -X POST https://staging.api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \\n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TEST' \\n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"splitstream-v1","input":"'"$(head -c 40000 /dev/urandom | base64)"'"}'
```
Maria Chen: on staging this returns slow tail and many small internal calls: logs show a lot of token-split events and subsequent KV cache misses. snippet: 
```
[2026-03-17T12:02:01Z] request_id=abcd token_split=46 subcalls=48 kvcache_hit=false latency_ms=1740
[2026-03-17T12:02:01Z] request_id=abcd batch_wait_ms=1020 exec_ms=600
```
Carmen Ruiz: looks like the tokenizer change produces many sub-tokens for long spans, causing the runtime to generate multiple sub-requests (splitstream). that increases queueing and defeats continuous batching heuristics.
Kevin Patel: hypothesis: batching window increases because worker prefetch expects larger chunks; with many subcalls we saturate fixed-size worker slots -> backpressure -> p99 spike. also KV cache keys differ per subcall so hit rate drops.
Ben Ortiz: can we test two quick mitigations: 1) force single-chunk tokenization in staging (fallback mode), 2) temporarily lower batching window to prefer lower latency over throughput.
Maria Chen: tried #1 on a canary — single-chunk fallback reduced median and p99 by ~40%. will push numbers to thread.
eng-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0317-72 assigned to eng-runtime.
Carmen Ruiz: short-term mitigation: rollback tokenizer change for onboarding customers + route affected customers to splitstream-v0.9. medium-term: change runtime to coalesce subcalls into single execution when input length > threshold, and normalize KV keys across splits.
Kevin Patel: also recommend adding a quick flag to disable split-based subrequests so support can flip per-customer. that buys time.
Ben Ortiz: I'll open a PR for the smaller batching window and a feature flag for split coalescing. cc @eng-runtime for review.
Maria Chen: customer comms: drafting message to impacted tenants offering rollout to v0.9 and ETA for extra mitigation.
Carmen Ruiz: tracking actions: rollback tokenizer change (maria), feature flag (ben), runtime coalesce design doc (kevin). update here when deployed. :thumbsup:
Maria Chen: deployed rollback to 10% canary at 12:45Z — initial metrics show p99 down to ~900ms on canary traffic. continuing rollout if stable.
Ben Ortiz: thanks — keep an eye on kvcache hit rate metric, and I'll add a dashboard for split-induced subcalls count.
Kevin Patel: if canary stays green, schedule full rollback. leaving this thread open for updates.
Maria Chen: noted. will post final once full rollback complete.
